canonical_record_policy.classification: MailEx event types describe communicative acts and event domains, not the FYP email-level multi-label taxonomy. Keep canonical labels empty and annotation.status unlabelled. Do not treat source events as FYP classification gold.
canonical_record_policy.text: Build raw_body, current_message, and clean_body by joining the source sentence tokens with single spaces. This is a token-joined reconstruction, not the original RFC822 message body. Preserve source event and argument annotations under annotation.source_annotations.
canonical_record_policy.metadata: The archive also contains plain-text raw_threads. Only copy From/To/CC/Subject/Date header values when message order and normalized body text align to the annotated turns. The files are not RFC822 messages and do not consistently provide metadata. Never infer attachment_names from body text.
canonical_record_policy.spans: Direct mappings are provisional, weak extraction proposals rather than FYP gold. Every emitted span requires human review for project scope and retains source role/event provenance. Keep classification labels empty and annotation.status unlabelled. MailEx records carry annotation.needs_review=true for downstream project-scope review.
canonical_record_policy.participant_suppression: Standalone first-, second-, and third-person pronouns and generic pronoun phrases in Meeting Members arguments remain in source annotations but are not emitted as canonical PARTICIPANT spans.

Request_Meeting.reason: A meeting proposal or request does not establish the FYP message category or project relevance.

Request_Meeting_Data.reason: A request for a meeting attribute may be a meeting-related email, but does not establish the FYP message category.

Deliver_Meeting_Data.reason: Providing meeting details is not enough to decide whether the entire email has the FYP MEETING label.

Amend_Meeting_Data.reason: A meeting amendment may be a change, cancellation, or another update and does not provide the FYP message label.

Request_Action.reason: An action request can cover many FYP categories, including approvals and follow-ups, so the event type is insufficient.

Request_Action_Data.reason: A question about an action is not necessarily a new action request or a follow-up.

Deliver_Action_Data.reason: A delivered action description may report completed work or acknowledge participation.

Request_Data.reason: Requested data can be a file, a fact, or another value; it does not always mean a report request.

Deliver_Data.reason: Delivered data can be a file or a fact and does not establish an FYP category.

Amend_Data.reason: Data amendments may describe many kinds of changes and do not establish a project status update.

Amend_Action_Data.reason: Preserve this observed rare source event type. Its argument semantics do not establish an FYP class.

Request_Action.reason: A requested action description is an action item candidate.

Request_Action_Data.reason: This event can ask for information about an existing action rather than request new work.

Deliver_Action_Data.reason: This event can report a completed action or acknowledge participation.

Amend_Action_Data.reason: This event describes an action amendment; the source does not identify pending-work status.

known_ontology_notes: The paper and repository summarize MailEx as having 10 event types. The downloaded full_data archive contains 11 observed non-O event keys, including 3 Amend_Action_Data instances. Preserve this observed type and report the source-count discrepancy.
MailEx labels arguments per event instance using BIO tags. Context and Revision qualifiers in Amend events must be retained because they distinguish the previous value from the proposed change.
MailEx event annotations may be useful for extraction pretraining, but its Enron business email domain and event taxonomy do not provide FYP gold labels.

All mapped spans are weak proposals, not FYP gold; review each message for whether its event belongs to a university project. Generic participant pronouns such as I and You guys are retained as source annotations but suppressed from canonical spans.
The archive has 776 O markers. Four occur alongside non-O event triggers, so only 772 turns are O-only; report marker and message counts separately.
